title: Adaptive session pinning with capacity-aware eviction and shadow rollback for geo/tier rollouts
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: As we scale staged model rollouts across regions and capacity tiers, current session pinning semantics (sticky affinity + TTL) cause two recurring issues: (1) prolonged hot-pinning that prevents safe progressive shifts when capacity is constrained; (2) unpredictable fallback churn when pinned variants are unavailable across tiers/regions. This ticket proposes an adaptive pinning and eviction system that considers capacity pressure, model-variant compatibility, and cost signals, plus a "shadow rollback" mode to validate rollback paths before user-visible switchovers.

Goals: 
- Allow safe, gradual traffic migration for canary/A-B rollouts while respecting tier priorities and geo stickiness.
- Minimize failed requests and latency spikes caused by naive pin eviction or cross-tier fallback.
- Provide observability and control hooks so SRE/PM can validate rollback paths without impacting live traffic.

Constraints and assumptions: 
- Existing request router supports region/tier ordering, version affinity, and TTL-based pin. We must not change the external API for customers.
- We cannot require immediate global re-keying of sessions; changes must be backward-compatible.
- Runtime must honor per-customer routing policies (pinned_version, prefer_tier, allowed_variants).

Proposal (high level): 
1) Adaptive pin score: maintain a small per-session score that decays over time but is increased/decreased by observed health/capacity signals. Score factors: age, recent successful requests, ticketed failure rate, current tier latency percentile, and per-variant cost multiplier. When score falls below threshold, session becomes eligible for soft-eviction.

2) Capacity-aware eviction: eviction decision is routed through a capacity oracle that returns a preference ordering for variants and tiers given current utilization and SLA targets. Soft-eviction moves the session into a probation routing bin where a fraction of requests (configurable) are served by the target rollout variant to test compatibility. Successful probation requests rebind session to new variant; failures increase session score (rebind to original).

3) Variant compatibility matrix: extend model metadata to include compatibility tags (e.g., tokenizer-hash, input-length-limit, structured-output-schema-id). Router will consult this matrix before routing across variants; incompatible sessions are diverted to fallback variants with explicit degradation notes.

4) Shadow rollback mode: new operator mode where rollback is executed in shadow for X% of affected sessions (configurable). Shadow rollback executes the rollback path without surfacing outputs to clients; results are recorded and compared against the live path using similarity metrics (exact-match for deterministic, fuzzy-match for generative). If shadow metrics exceed thresholds, automated rollback can be promoted to live with a one-click flow in Console.

5) Observability: Add per-session traces for pin transitions, probation outcomes, and shadow comparisons. Expose new Console panels: "Pin churn heatmap", "Probation success rate", and "Shadow rollback delta" with drilldowns by region/tier/variant. Alerting rules: probation-success-rate < 95% for >5m; shadow-delta > threshold for >10m.

Technical changes required: 
- Router: new state machine for session pin: {Pinned, Probation, Unpinned} + score update hooks. Implemented in routing-resolver module.
- Capacity oracle: lightweight API backed by metrics from autoscaler and a simple cost model. Schema: /oracle/preference?region=...&tier=... returns ordered list of variant+tier pairs.
- Model metadata extension: add compatibility_tags and cost_multiplier fields to catalog entries. Migration plan: catalog update RPC + backward compatibility default (empty tags = any).
- Console: add UI controls for enabling shadow rollback, tuning probation fraction, and visualizing per-session outcomes.
- SDK/Telemetry: add session-level tags to traces and extend audit logs when pin transitions occur.

Simulation & early experiments: 
- Ran a simulated canary (5% traffic) with synthetic session populations across 3 regions and 2 tiers (standard/premium). Key findings: probation reduces median latency spikes by ~28% vs immediate rebind under 90th percentile tail pressure; shadow rollback detected a semantic regression in 3% of sessions that was not visible via aggregate token-level metrics.
- Cost model: adaptive pinning reduced cross-tier fallback volume by 41% in the experiment, lowering estimated per-token bill by ~6% for the customer cohort.

Open questions / trade-offs: 
- Probation sample size: default 10% may be insufficient for rare regressions; but increasing sample size lengthens exposure window. We propose parameterizing per-rollout.
- Complexity vs debuggability: third state (Probation) increases router complexity and state churn; we must ensure state machine is well-instrumented and bounded.
- Shadow fidelity: similarity metrics for generative models are heuristic; false positives may block legitimate rollbacks. We need to iterate on chosen metrics and expose tuning knobs.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Router implements new pin-state machine and respects capacity oracle preference in 95% of synthetic tests.
- Console shows probation/success rate and shadow-rollout delta; alerts fire under configured SLO breaches.
- No customer-facing API changes; migrations to catalog OK with default compatibility tags.
- Experiment demonstrates reduced latency spikes and fallback volume in staging.

Rollout plan: 
1) Internal prototype behind feature flag (router + catalog + telemetry) — target: runtime-1.25-alpha.
2) Staging trials: enable for non-critical orgs and run canary and shadow rollback on selected rollouts for 2 weeks.
3) Gradual enablement by default for new rollouts; manual opt-in for existing pinned sessions for 4 weeks, then auto-evaluate.
4) Full GA after 8 weeks and successful SRE signoff.

Action items / next steps: 
- ENG: implement pin-state machine and capacity oracle shim (owners: Liam Chen, Priya Kapoor) — PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1789
- PM: define probation default parameters per tier and document in Console (owner: Noah Patel) — doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ROLL-ADAPTIVE-PINNING
- DX: design Console panels for shadow rollout and probation (owner: Maya Singh) — Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/rollouts-shadow-ux
- SRE: create alert runbook for probation failures and shadow drift (owner: Emma Johnson) — runbook link: https://runbooks.internal.redwood/sre/rollout-probation

Notes: This ticket intentionally couples routing logic with observability and operator flows to reduce unknowns during rollouts. The shadow rollback mode is reversible and should significantly lower the risk of accidental user-impacting rollbacks.
